c74object.name: bachmcp.pshmbuffer~
c74object.digest: A polybuffer~ of shared memories, for Python to read and write
c74object.description: Like polybuffer~, it holds buffers named <name>.1, <name>.2 ... <name>.<count>: in Max they are buffer~ objects (groove~ pepe.3 plays the third), and each one has a shared memory of the same name that another program, notably Python (PShmBuffer in py/bach_mcp/utilities/shmbuffer.py), reads and writes: each is a plain bachmcp.shmbuffer~ memory, so ShmBuffer("pepe.3") is the third. A small index memory under the name itself says how many there are; <name> alone is not a buffer~, as with polybuffer~. The buffer~s exist in Max as soon as their memories do; a buffer~ of that name already in a patch is used, not duplicated. Python may add memories, remove the last one, resize or rewrite any: the object follows on the next message, and at once with notify 1. No audio: the buffer~s hold what plays.

inlet.digest: bang, int: memories into buffer~s; load, append, remove, source, target, write, info

outlet.digest: bang when done; count; info; written

objarg.name: name
objarg.description: The memories are /bachmcp.<name>.<n> and the index /bachmcp.<name>: at most 17 characters, no slash. With a name only, the object joins the memories if a program already made them, or starts with none.

objarg.name: count
objarg.description: With a count, the object makes that many new, silent memories (0 to 9999), replacing what was under the name.

objarg.name: ms
objarg.description: The duration of each new memory, at Max's sample rate. Default 0.

method.name: bang
method.digest: Write every memory to its buffer~
method.description: Writes each memory into its buffer~ (the object's own <name>.<n>, or target's), resized to fit. Then a bang out of the right outlet and <name> <count> out of the left one (the target's name when there is one).

method.name: load
method.digest: Memory n becomes a sound file or a buffer~
method.description: Memory n becomes this sound file (any format macOS reads: wav, aiff, caf, mp3, m4a, flac ...; absolute, or a name in Max's search path) or a copy of this buffer~, with its format. n = count + 1 adds one at the end.

method.name: readfolder
method.digest: Add every sound file of a folder
method.description: Every sound file in the folder, sorted by name, added at the end, as polybuffer~ does. loadfolder is the same.

method.name: appendempty
method.description: Adds <name>.<count+1>, silent, of this duration and channels (default 1).

method.name: append
method.digest: One more memory, a copy of a buffer~
method.description: Adds <name>.<count+1>, a copy of this buffer~.

method.name: remove
method.description: Only the last can be removed: the names stay .1 to .<count>.

method.name: clear
method.description: The count becomes 0; the index stays.

method.name: source
method.digest: Read the memories from somewhere, now
method.description: The same as source, and it reads at once.

method.name: target
method.digest: Write the memories into a polybuffer~, now
method.description: The same as target, and it writes at once. Alone: no target; the object's own buffer~s again.

method.name: set_name
method.description: Memories already under the new name: the object joins them. None: its memories come along (<name>.1 ...), and the old ones are removed if this object made them. name is the same.

method.name: getcount
method.description: count <n> out of the right outlet.

method.name: info
method.digest: Report the index, or memory n
method.description: Out of the right outlet, one message each. Alone: name, shm (the index's name for shm_open), count, serial. With n: name (<name>.<n>), shm, frames, channels, sr, ms, serial.

method.name: write
method.digest: Write memory n into a sound file
method.description: As buffer~ does: the format comes from the extension (.wav .aif .caf .flac; none: .wav), the sample type from samptype. No file: a save dialog. A bare name goes next to the patcher. Then written <n> <path> out of the right outlet.

method.name: writetofolder
method.digest: Write every memory into a folder
method.description: Every memory as <name>.<n>.wav (or aiff, flac, caf), as polybuffer~ does; the folder is made if missing. Then written <count> <folder> out of the right outlet.

attribute.name: source
attribute.description: Looked up in this order: a polybuffer~ (buffers <source>.1, <source>.2 ... until one is missing): as many memories as its buffers, with their formats; a buffer~: one memory, a copy; a folder: one memory per sound file, sorted by name; a sound file: one memory. Given as an argument, it is read once the patcher is loaded.

attribute.name: target
attribute.digest: The polybuffer~ the memories go to
attribute.description: A polybuffer~ written instead of the object's own buffer~s: memory n into <target>.<n>. It must already hold as many buffers (appendempty): the object can't add buffers to another polybuffer~.

attribute.name: notify
attribute.digest: Write when Python says it changed something
attribute.description: 1: when the other program announces a change (in Python: touch() on the set or on a member, append(), pop(), clear(), which post the Darwin notification bachmcp.shmbuffer.<name>), write the memories that changed, and make buffer~s for new ones. Nothing is polled. Either way, the Max console says python written <name>.

c74object.discussion: The index is a 64-byte shared memory holding the count and a serial (layout in sources/bachmcp.shmbuffer~/source/bachmcp.shmbuffer.h); whoever adds a memory makes it first, then raises the count. In Python: poly = PShmBuffer("name"); len(poly); poly[2].array, the samples of the second (from 1, as polybuffer~; negative from the end); poly[2].touch(); poly.append(samples, sr=48000); poly.pop(); poly.wait(), which sleeps until Max changes the set (appendempty, append, load, remove, clear, source). There is no lock. The memories and the index are removed when the object that made the index is freed. Messages run in the main thread. examples/python/shmbuffers.py, run by bachmcp.python, shows the Python side.
